source_text: Ὅτι δὲ Μωϋσῆς εἶπεν: Οὐ φάγεσθε χοῖρον οὔτε ἀετὸν οὔτε ὀξύπτερον οὔτε κόρακα οὔτε πάντα ἰχθύν, ὃς οὐκ ἔχει λεπίδα ἐν ἑαυτῷ, τρία ἔλαβεν ἐν τῇ συνέσει δόγματα. πέρας γέ τοι λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν τῷ Δευτερονομίῳ: Καὶ διαθήσομαι πρὸς τὸν λαὸν τοῦτον τὰ δικαιώματά μου. ἄρα οὖν οὐκ ἔστιν ἐντολὴ θεοῦ τὸ μὴ τρώγειν, Μωϋσῆς δὲ ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν. τὸ οὖν χοιρίον πρὸς τοῦτο εἶπεν: οὐ κολληθήσῃ φησίν, ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινές εἰσιν ὅμοιοι χοίρων: τουτέστιν ὅταν σπαταλῶσιν, ἐπιλανθάνονται τοῦ κυρίου, ὅταν δὲ ὑστεροῦνται, ἐπιγινώσκουσιν τὸν κύριον, ὡς καὶ ὁ χοῖρος ὅταν τρώγει τὸν κύριον οὐκ οἶδεν, ὅταν δὲ πεινᾷ κραυγάζει, καὶ λαβὼν πάλιν σιωπᾷ. Οὐδὲ φάγῃ τὸν ἀετὸν οὐδὲ τὸν ὀξύπτερον οὐδὲ τὸν ἰκτῖνα οὐδὲ τὸν κόρακα: οὐ μή, φησίν, κολληθήσῃ οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες οὐκ οἴδασιν διὰ κόπου καὶ ἱδρῶτος πορίζειν ἑαυτοῖς τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἁρπάζουσιν τὰ ἀλλότρια ἐν ἀνομίᾳ αὐτῶν καὶ ἐπιτηροῦσιν ὡς ἐν ἀκεραιοσύνῃ περιπατοῦντες καὶ περιβλέπονται, τίνα ἐκδύσωσιν διὰ τὴν πλεονεξίαν, ὡς καὶ τὰ ὄρνεα ταῦτα μόνα ἑαυτοῖς οὐ προίζει τὴν τροφήν, ἀλλὰ ἀργὰ καθήμενα ἐκζητεῖ, πῶς ἀλλοτρίας σάρκας καταφάγῃ, ὄντα λοιμὰ τῇ πονηρίᾳ αὐτῶν. Καὶ οὐ φάγῃ, φησίν, σμύραιναν οὐδὲ πολύποδα οὐδὲ σηπίαν: οὐ μή, φησίν, ὁμοιωθήσῃ κολλώμενος ἀνθρώποις τοιούτοις, οἵτινες εἰς τέλος εἰσὶν ἀσεβεῖς καὶ κεκριμένοι ἤδη τῷ θανάτῳ, ὡς καὶ ταῦτα τὰ ἰχθύδια μόνα ἐπικατάρατα ἐν τῷ βυθῷ νήχεται, μὴ κολυμβῶντα ὡς τὰ λοιπά, ἀλλ’ ἐν τῇ γῇ κάτω τοῦ βυθοῦ κατοικεῖ. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὸν δασύποδα οὐ φάγῃ. πρὸς τί; οὐ μὴ γένῃ, φησίν, παιδοφθόρος οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις, ὅτι ὁ λαγωὸς κατ’ ἐνιαυτὸν πλεονεκτεῖ τὴν ἀφόδευσιν: ὅσα γὰρ ἔτη ζῇ, τοσαύτας ἔχει τρύπας. ἀλλὰ οὐδὲ τὴν ὕαιναν φάγῃ: οὐ μή, φησίν, γένῃ μοιχὸς οὐδὲ φθορεὺς οὐδὲ ὁμοιωθήσῃ τοῖς τοιούτοις. πρὸς τί; ὅτι τὸ ζῷον τοῦτο παρ ἐνιαυτὸν ἀλλάσσει τὴν φύσιν καὶ ποτὲ μὲν ἄρρεν, ποτὲ δὲ θῆλυ γίνεται. ἀλλὰ καὶ τὴν γαλῆν ἐμίσησεν καλῶς. οὐ μή, φησίν, γενηθῇς τοιοῦτος, οἵους ἀκούομεν ἀνομίαν ποιοῦντας ἐν τῷ στόματι δἰ ἀκαθαρσίαν, οὐδὲ κολληθήσῃ ταῖς ἀκαθάρτοις ταῖς τὴν ἀνομίαν ποιούσαις ἐν τῷ στόματι. τὸ γὰρ ζῷον τοῦτο τῷ στόματι κύει. περὶ μὲν τῶν βρωμάτων λαβὼν Μωϋσῆς τρία δόγματα οὕτως ἐν πνεύματι ἐλάλησεν: οἱ δὲ κατ’ ἐπιθυμίαν τῆς σαρκὸς ὡς περὶ βρώσεως προσεδέξαντο. λαμβάνει δὲ τῶν αὐτῶν τριῶν δογμάτων γνῶσιν Δαυείδ καὶ λέγει: Μακάριος ἀνήρ, ὃς οὐκ ἐπορεύθη ἐν βουλῇ ἀσεβῶν, καθὼς καὶ οἱ ἰχθύες πορεύονται ἐν σκότει εἰς τὰ βάθη: καὶ ἐν ὁδῷ ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἔστη, καθὼς οἱ δοκοῦντες φοβεῖσθαι τὸν κύριον ἁμαρτάνουσιν ὡς ὁ χοῖρος, καὶ ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν οὐκ ἐκάθισεν, καθὼς τὰ πετεινὰ καθήμενα εἰς ἁρπαγήν. ἔχετε τελείως καὶ περὶ τῆς βρώσεως. πάλιν λέγει Μωϋσῆς: Φάγεσθε πᾶν διχηλοῦν καὶ μαρυκώμενον. τί λέγει; ὅτι τὴν τροφὴν λαμβάνων οἶδεν τὸν τρέφοντα αὐτὸν καὶ ἐπ’ αὐτῷ ἀναπαυόμενος εὐφραίνεσθαι δοκεῖ. καλῶς εἶπεν βλέπων τὴν ἐντολήν. τί οὖν λέγει; κολλᾶσθε μετὰ τῶν φοβουμένων τὸν κύριον, μετὰ τῶν μελετώντων ὃ ἔλαβον διάσταλμα ῥήματος ἐν τῇ καρδίᾳ, μετὰ τῶν λαλούντων τὰ διδαιώματα κυρίου καὶ τηρούντων, μετὰ τῶν εἰδότων, ὅτι ἡ μελέτη ἐστὶν ἔργον εὐφροσύνης, καὶ ἀναμαρυκωμένων τὸν λόγον κυρίου. τί δὲ τὸ διχηλοῦν; ὅτι ὁ δίκαιος καὶ ἐν τούτῳ τῷ κόσμῳ περιπατεῖ καὶ τὸν ἅγιον αἰῶνα ἐκδέχεται. βλέπετε, πῶς ἐνομοθέτησεν Μωϋσῆς καλῶς. ἀλλὰ πόθεν ἐκείνοις ταῦτα νοῆσαι ἢ συνιέναι; ἡμεῖς δὲ δικαίως νοήσαντες τὰς ἐντολὰς λαλοῦμεν, ὡς ἠθέλησεν ὁ κύριος. διὰ τοῦτο περιέτεμεν τὰς ἀκοὰς ἡμῶν καὶ τὰς καρδίας, ἵνα συνιῶμεν ταῦτα.
pass_a_gloss: For Moses said: You will not eat pig nor eagle nor oxypeter nor crow nor all fish which does not have a scale in itself, he took three doctrines in wisdom. For he says to them in Deuteronomy: And I will make a covenant with this people concerning my ordinances. Therefore it is not a command of God not to eat, but Moses spoke in spirit. Therefore concerning the pig he said: You will not be glued, he says, to such people, who are similar to pigs: that is when they squander, they forget the Lord, when they are in need, they recognize the Lord, just as the pig when it eats does not know the Lord, when it is hungry it cries out, and having eaten again it is silent. You will not eat the eagle nor the oxypeter nor the fish nor the crow: not, he says, will you be glued or likened to such people, who do not know how to provide food for themselves through labor and sweat, but seize the things of others in their lawlessness and watch as if walking in uncleanness and looking around, whom they may strip through greed, just as these birds alone do not provide food for themselves, but sitting idly they seek how they may eat the flesh of others, being polluted by their wickedness. And you will not eat, he says, the smyrnian nor the polypod nor the cuttlefish: not, he says, will you be likened by being glued to such people, who are ungodly and already judged to death, just as these little fish are alone cursed in the deep, not swimming as the others, but dwelling on the ground below the deep. But also you will not eat the dasypus. Why? Not, he says, will you become a corrupter of children nor be likened to such, because the hare each year oversteps its burrow: for as many years as it lives, it has that many holes. But also you will not eat the hyena: not, he says, will you become an adulterer nor a corrupter nor be likened to such. Why? Because this animal changes its nature each year and sometimes is male, sometimes female. But also he rightly hated the cat. Not, he says, will you become such, who we hear are doing lawlessness with the mouth through uncleanness, nor will you be glued to the unclean ones who do lawlessness with the mouth. For this animal conceives with the mouth. Concerning foods Moses took three doctrines and thus spoke in spirit: but they according to the desire of the flesh received it as concerning eating. But David receives knowledge of the same three doctrines and says: Blessed is the man who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly, just as the fish walk in darkness into the depths: and in the way of sinners he did not stand, just as those who seem to fear the Lord sin like the pig, and on the seat of the polluted ones he did not sit, just as the birds sitting for plunder. You have it completely concerning eating. Again Moses says: Eat every split and chewed thing. What does he say? That taking food, one knows the one who nourishes him and resting on him seems to rejoice. He spoke well, seeing the command. What then does he say? Be glued with those who fear the Lord, with those who meditate on what they received as a word of separation in the heart, with those who speak the teachings of the Lord and keep them, with those who know that meditation is a work of joy, and who chew the word of the Lord. What is the split thing? That the righteous both walks in this world and awaits the holy age. See how Moses legislated well. But from where will they understand these things or comprehend? We, having understood the commands rightly, speak as the Lord willed. Therefore we have circumcised our ears and hearts, so that we may comprehend these things.

pass_b_english: Moses gave a command about what foods to eat, but it's not just about food - it's about the kind of people we should be. He said, 'Don't eat pig, eagle, oxypeter, crow, or any fish without scales,' and in doing so, he taught us three important principles. As he said in Deuteronomy, God makes a covenant with His people to give them His ordinances (Deuteronomy). So, it's not that God is commanding us not to eat certain foods, but rather Moses is speaking to us in a spiritual way. When it comes to pigs, Moses is warning us against being like people who waste what they have and only remember God when they're in need. Just like a pig that eats without knowing its master and only cries out when it's hungry, these people only turn to God when they're struggling. We shouldn't be like that. Moses also tells us not to eat eagles, oxypeters, fish, or crows. He's saying we shouldn't be like people who don't work hard to provide for themselves, but instead take what belongs to others and live sinful lives, always looking for their next victim to exploit. These birds are a great example of this - they don't work to find their own food, but instead sit around waiting for an easy meal, and in doing so, they become polluted by their own wickedness. Additionally, Moses warns us against eating certain sea creatures, like the smyrnian, polypod, or cuttlefish. He's telling us not to be like people who are ungodly and destined for death, just like these sea creatures that live in the depths of the ocean, separate from the rest. He also warns us against eating the dasypus, a type of hare, because it's known for overstepping its boundaries and living a life of excess. And we shouldn't eat the hyena, an animal that changes its nature from male to female, because we shouldn't be like people who are unfaithful and corrupt. Moses even hated the cat, an animal that conceives through its mouth, because we shouldn't be like people who use their words to sin and corrupt others. Moses taught us these principles, but the people only understood them in a physical sense, as rules about what to eat. However, David understood the spiritual significance of these teachings and wrote, 'Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of the scornful' - just like the fish that swim in the dark depths of the ocean, or the birds that sit waiting for their prey. Moses also taught us to eat foods that are split and chewed, symbolizing the way we should meditate on God's word and rejoice in His presence. He's telling us to surround ourselves with people who fear God, who meditate on His word, and who keep His teachings. We should be like the righteous, who live in this world but look forward to the holy age to come. Moses gave us these teachings, but it's up to us to understand them. We have circumcised our hearts and ears to comprehend the commands of God, and we speak as the Lord has willed.

Moses' teachings are not just about following rules, but about living a life that honors God. When he says, 'Eat every split and chewed thing,' he's not just talking about food - he's talking about the way we should approach God's word. We should be people who meditate on His teachings, who rejoice in His presence, and who live according to His principles. The 'split thing' represents the righteous person, who lives in this world but looks forward to the holy age to come. Moses legislated well, but it's up to us to understand the spiritual significance of his teachings. We can't just follow the rules without understanding the heart behind them. That's why we've circumcised our hearts and ears, so that we can comprehend the commands of God and live according to His will. By doing so, we can be the people God has called us to be, and we can live a life that honors Him.

review.notes: Pass B is a paraphrase/summary rather than a translation, which violates the requirement that a summary is not a translation. Specifically, Pass B omits several specific animal names and detailed descriptions present in the Greek and Pass A, such as the specific reasoning for the 'dasypus' (the hare's holes) and the 'hyena' (changing nature), and it significantly compresses the text into a narrative form. Furthermore, Pass B introduces a scripture citation for the Davidic quote (Psalm 1:1) as 'Blessed is the man who does not walk in the counsel of the wicked, nor stand in the way of sinners, nor sit in the seat of the scornful', whereas the Greek text (and Pass A) provides a different sequence and wording: 'Blessed is the man, who did not walk in the counsel of the ungodly... and in the way of sinners he did not stand... and on the seat of the polluted ones he did not sit' (Μακάριος ἀνήρ, ὃς οὐκ ἐπορεύθη ἐν βουλῇ ἀσεβῶν... καὶ ἐν ὁδῷ ἁμαρτωλῶν οὐκ ἔστη... καὶ ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν οὐκ ἐκάθισεν). Pass B's version is a standard liturgical/KJV-style rendering of Psalm 1:1, which is not what the Greek text actually says.
reasons: Pass B is a summary/paraphrase, not a translation, omitting significant clauses and details from the Greek (e.g., the specific description of the hare's holes: 'ὅσα γὰρ ἔτη ζῇ, τοσαύτας ἔχει τρύπας').

Pass B alters the wording of the Davidic quote to match a standard Psalm 1:1 translation rather than the specific Greek text provided: 'ἐπὶ καθέδραν λοιμῶν οὐκ ἐκάθισεν' (on the seat of the polluted ones he did not sit) vs Pass B 'nor sit in the seat of the scornful'.
